purpose: Source-traceable buried P&T/DUR/PDL document insights for pharma companies.

insights.insight_title: Final PDL authority sits with DOM leadership, while net cost and rebate pool leverage are explicit inputs
insights.why_it_matters: Committee votes are not the final coverage action. Manufacturers need to track the Medicaid Executive Director approval step, the 30-day notice/go-live cycle, and Mississippi's reliance on supplemental rebates through the Sovereign States Drug Consortium.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: DOM states that committee recommendation and net cost are both considered; DOM aggressively pursues supplemental rebates through the SSDC pool. Committee votes and MedImpact preferred/non-preferred recommendations go to the Medicaid Executive Director for final approval, with public notice 30 days before the new PDL goes live.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in May 13, 2025 Mississippi P&T minutes; the February 10, 2026 draft minutes restate the same governance pattern.

insights.insight_title: Vykat XR access requires genetic confirmation plus hyperphagia evidence and response-based renewal
insights.drug_or_class: Vykat XR (diazoxide choline) for Prader-Willi syndrome
insights.why_it_matters: The access hurdle is not merely diagnosis. TennCare requires medical records supporting methylation analysis and hyperphagia symptoms, then renewal evidence of response, creating a high-documentation pathway for a rare-disease launch.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The criteria require age at least 4, Prader-Willi syndrome, chart-note submission documenting methylation analysis genetic testing and hyperphagia signs or symptoms, and specialist prescribing or consultation. Renewal requires positive clinical response such as decreased hunger, reduced food consumption, improved satiety, fewer food preoccupations, BMI improvement, or metabolic-marker improvement.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 406-424; page marker is Page 8.

insights.insight_title: Migraine CGRP step burden explicitly changes if supplemental rebates lapse
insights.why_it_matters: The access barrier is not just clinical; rebate participation is directly tied to whether preferred CGRP products require two or three prior preventive therapy failures.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The packet states that Ajovy and Emgality manufacturers provided supplemental rebates to be preferred CGRP inhibitors and require trials with two other migraine preventive therapies; if they do not participate in supplemental rebates, they revert to original criteria requiring trials with three other therapies.
insights.validation_note: Verified in packet text lines 8791-8800; page marker shows Page 211.

insights.insight_title: PDL recommendations are not final until DHHS Secretary approval, with a 30-day comment cycle
insights.why_it_matters: Monitoring should not stop at Review Panel votes; there is a formal Secretary approval step and a quarterly cadence that can affect implementation timing.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The October 2025 minutes state that the 2023 law established quarterly PDL Review Panel meetings, a public comment period, and a procedure for Review Panel recommendations to the Secretary of DHHS; the public comment period is 30 days, and recommendations approved by the panel are submitted to the DHHS Secretary for final approval.
insights.validation_note: Verified in minutes text lines 50-64; page marker shows Page 1.

insights.insight_title: Wyoming's oral JAK pathway for alopecia requires 90-day topical steroid failure, SALT >50%, and dermatology consultation
insights.drug_or_class: Leqselvi and oral JAK inhibitors for alopecia areata; Opzelura for vitiligo
insights.why_it_matters: The state treated alopecia areata and vitiligo as medical conditions, but created severity and specialist gates for oral JAKs and sent the class for cost analysis and PDL placement.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The committee noted adult alopecia is not otherwise a covered diagnosis but EPSDT can cover children, then moved to treat alopecia areata and vitiligo as medical conditions. It required failure of a high-potency corticosteroid for at least 90 days, SALT score greater than 50%, and dermatologist consultation before oral JAK approval, with oral JAKs referred for cost analysis and PDL placement.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 119-145; page marker is Page 3.

insights.insight_title: Wisconsin committee recommendations go to the DHS Secretary for adoption, modification, or referral back
insights.why_it_matters: Committee action is not the final implementation step. Manufacturers should track secretary-level adoption or modification rather than assuming meeting recommendations are final policy.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The PAC guidelines state that committee recommendations are presented to the Secretary for adoption, modification, or referral back to the Division of Medicaid Services for further action or review.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 477-480; page marker is Page 9.

insights.insight_title: Non-preferred wakefulness drugs require only one preferred failure, while Uzedy gets a pediatric PA carveout
insights.why_it_matters: South Carolina exposes different access levers in one meeting: a relatively shallow one-preferred-agent step for anti-narcolepsy agents and an age-based PA trigger for a long-acting antipsychotic.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: August 2025 minutes add armodafinil and modafinil generics as preferred and Nuvigil, Provigil, Sunosi, and Wakix as non-preferred, with all non-preferred medications requiring trial and failure of one preferred agent plus clinical criteria. The same minutes add Uzedy as preferred but require prior authorizations for children less than or equal to 6 years of age; the class changes were effective Jan. 1, 2026.
insights.validation_note: Verified in August 2025 minutes text lines 128-135, 155-168, and 176-179; page markers show Pages 3-4.

insights.insight_title: DURB recommendations move from public comment to clinical review to cost review before Commissioner selection
insights.why_it_matters: NYRx preferred status is not purely a public clinical vote; cost information enters after public comment and clinical research, and the Commissioner is the final selection point.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The PDP page says DURB reviews drug classes and makes recommendations to the Commissioner of Health on preferred and non-preferred drugs and clinical criteria for non-preferred PA. Recommendations are based on public comment and testimony, objective clinical research, then drug cost information. Upcoming board activities are posted 30 days prior to meetings.
insights.validation_note: Verified in extracted HTML around the Commissioner and DURB description; HTML source has no page numbers.

insights.insight_title: Rezdiffra step edit was modified to allow specialist justification when Wegovy is expected ineffective
insights.why_it_matters: This is a precise Board-level amendment to a proposed criteria package. It creates a pathway around a Wegovy step requirement for Rezdiffra when specialist justification supports it.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: In October 2025 minutes, Prime presented MASH criteria for Wegovy and Rezdiffra. The Board approved Rezdiffra criteria with added statement to the step-edit requirement allowing a specialist-justification option if there is reason to expect Wegovy to be ineffective for the recipient's specific treatment; Wegovy criteria were approved separately.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Nevada October 16, 2025 DUR minutes; MCO medical directors approved proposed criteria as presented before Board amendment.

insights.insight_title: Kansas approved Niemann-Pick C PA while keeping miglustat step therapy on the table until July 2026 review
insights.why_it_matters: For NPC entrants, the near-term barrier is not just diagnosis confirmation; a legacy miglustat step requirement was important enough for manufacturer comment and a scheduled re-review.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Kansas minutes say Aqneursa and Miplyffa PA criteria were proposed for FDA-label appropriate use; IntraBio requested removal of step therapy with miglustat; the Board requested review at the July 2026 DUR meeting and noted the state can defer discussion if there is no utilization.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 309-326; page marker is Page4 at line 276.

insights.insight_title: Connecticut Medicaid step therapy is statutorily capped at one preferred-drug failure and excludes mental-health drugs
insights.why_it_matters: Manufacturers can use the statutory limit to challenge over-sequenced criteria: step therapy cannot require multiple preferred failures and must offer expedited overrides for medical necessity or expected harm.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The State Law Requirements document says step therapy may require trying and failing only one preferred-list drug, does not apply to mental-health-related drugs, and must provide an expedited override when the preferred treatment failed, is expected to be ineffective, likely causes harm, or medical necessity supports the requested drug.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 37-57; PDF extraction lacks explicit page marker, but all cited text is on the first extracted page.

insights.insight_title: Alaska separates manufacturer clinical submissions from general public comments and enforces a much earlier manufacturer deadline
insights.why_it_matters: Manufacturers need to engage before the public-comment window; the January 2026 manufacturer deadline was 14 days before the meeting, while general submissions were due two days before the meeting.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: For the January 16, 2026 P&T meeting, the notice says manufacturer clinical submissions were accepted until January 2, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. AK time; public materials were requested by January 14, 2026 for inclusion.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 10-22; page marker is Page 1.

insights.insight_title: Wyoming's Wegovy MASH criteria require recent fibrosis evidence and block GLP-1 duplication
insights.why_it_matters: The criteria turn a broad MASH indication into a liver-staging and duplication-control pathway. Market access should anticipate biopsy/NIT timing, F2/F3 restriction, and renewal tied to avoiding F4 progression.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Wyoming approved Wegovy for MASH with diagnosis confirmed by liver biopsy within the previous three years or noninvasive testing within the past six months, baseline F2 or F3 fibrosis, prescriber attestation of diet and exercise, and no use with GLP-1 receptor agonists or GLP-1 combination products. Reauthorization requires no progression to F4 and continued diet/exercise; approval duration is 12 months.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 71-97; page marker is Page 2.

insights.insight_title: Cytokine/CAM antagonists face all-preferred-agent trials and biosimilar cost steering
insights.drug_or_class: Cytokine and CAM antagonists, including anti-TNFs and related biologics
insights.why_it_matters: Grandfathering is conditional, not automatic. A stabilized patient can still be redirected if a more cost-effective biosimilar exists, and off-label use goes to medical-director review.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Non-preferred Cytokine/CAM antagonists require 90-day trials of all preferred agents indicated for the diagnosis unless an exception applies. Patients stable for at least six months may be grandfathered only for labeled use and only if a more cost-effective biosimilar is not available. If a biosimilar exists but is also non-preferred, the PA vendor advises the provider which product is most cost-effective; all off-label requests require medical-director review.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 2767-2772; page marker is Page 31.

insights.insight_title: Washington excludes new drug information not reviewed by DERP and uses the TOP$ supplemental rebate pool
insights.drug_or_class: All P&T/DUR agenda classes; Medicaid supplemental rebates
insights.why_it_matters: A manufacturer may have only three minutes to speak, and evidence outside DERP review cannot be considered by the committee. Rebate strategy is also routed through the TOP$ pool administered by Provider Synergies/Prime.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The meetings page says stakeholders receive three minutes for comments, written testimony is limited to a two-page letter at least one week before the meeting, and new drug information not reviewed by the Drug Effectiveness Review Project cannot be considered. It also states HCA joined The Optimal PDL Solution (TOP$) supplemental rebate pool effective January 1, 2018, administered by Provider Synergies, a Prime Therapeutics subsidiary.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local HTML text on the meetings page; page_number is null because the source is HTML.

insights.insight_title: Vermont's denial and rebate data show off-label GLP-1 use and MDRP exits as operational pressure points
insights.therapeutic_area: Cross-therapeutic pharmacy benefit; obesity; branded drugs
insights.drug_or_class: GLP-1s for weight loss; branded drugs discontinued from MDRP
insights.why_it_matters: The report connects utilization management outcomes to concrete denial drivers and net-cost strategy, giving manufacturers a read on where access friction is occurring.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Vermont reported 28,267 PA requests in SFY25 with a 33.1% denial rate. Denials were attributed in part to off-label GLP-1 weight-loss requests and branded drugs discontinued from the Medicaid Drug Rebate Program, with providers directed to rebated or guideline-based alternatives. The report also says drugs with substantial federal rebates may be preferred because of lower net state cost.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text around lines 310-320 and 372-390; page markers are Pages 6-7.

insights.insight_title: TennCare's weight-management GLP-1 criteria were explicitly budget-driven and include early renewal loss thresholds
insights.drug_or_class: Saxenda, Wegovy, and Zepbound for weight management
insights.why_it_matters: The buried signal is that utilization pressure, not only clinical evidence, triggered tighter criteria. Manufacturers should model early discontinuation risk because renewal requires documented weight loss and nonresponders get only a short titration-off window.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: TennCare said increased utilization over the prior three months raised concern about exceeding budgetary restrictions. Proposed weight-management criteria included lifestyle-program participation, no combination with other obesity/weight-loss medications, Saxenda failure of two preferred agents, and renewal documentation of at least 3% weight loss at the month-3 renewal or at least 5% for later renewals, with up to one month to titrate off if criteria are not met.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 542-545 and 621-630; page markers are Pages 11-12.

insights.insight_title: DUR public comment is in-person only, capped, and constrained to one speaker per manufacturer
insights.why_it_matters: Manufacturers cannot rely on virtual attendance or multiple aligned speakers; the practical window opens only after agenda posting and closes 24 hours before the meeting.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Speaker registration forms must be received after agenda posting and no later than 24 hours before the meeting; public comment is capped at 40 total minutes, each speaker gets 5 minutes if eight or fewer speakers register, only one speaker per manufacturer is allowed, and public comment through Zoom is not allowed.
insights.validation_note: Verified in agenda text lines 81-97; page marker shows Page 2.

insights.insight_title: Line-extension muscle relaxants show extreme unit-cost scrutiny before PA votes
insights.drug_or_class: Tanlor, metaxalone 640 mg, Zanaflex 8 mg, methocarbamol and tizanidine formulations
insights.why_it_matters: Formulation and strength launches can trigger PA even where older generics share the indication and dose logic; dossiers should anticipate formulation-substitution and cost-per-day comparisons.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The February 2026 packet compares Tanlor 1,000 mg at $2,820 per 30 days with methocarbamol 500 mg at $7.20 and 750 mg at $6.00, and compares metaxalone 640 mg at $7,500 per 30 days with metaxalone 800 mg at $60.00; costs are based on NADAC, WAC, or SMAC and do not reflect rebates or net costs.
insights.validation_note: Verified in packet text lines 7104-7131 and 7170-7193; page markers show Pages 127-128.

insights.insight_title: Manufacturer presentations are clinical-only, Friday-confirmed, and written materials are due two business days before vote
insights.why_it_matters: Ohio permits manufacturer presentation, but the format excludes price discussion and imposes short, specific timing gates before committee votes.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Ohio bylaws say manufacturers whose products are under review may present or submit written material but should focus on relative clinical merits and not discuss price or committee business with members outside the public meeting. Requests to present must be received by 5:00 pm on the Friday before the meeting, presentations are limited to three minutes, and written materials should be submitted electronically at least two business days before the meeting.
insights.validation_note: Verified in bylaws text lines 146-205; page marker shows Page 4.

insights.insight_title: MASH criteria make Rezdiffra step through semaglutide, with pioglitazone added for type 2 diabetes
insights.why_it_matters: The MASH access path favors older or broader metabolic therapies before a branded MASH-specific agent, and renewal requires histologic or noninvasive evidence of response.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: For Rezdiffra, concurrent type 2 diabetes requires failure of a 6-month trial of semaglutide combined with pioglitazone; without type 2 diabetes, failure of a 6-month semaglutide trial is required. Renewal requires resolution of steatohepatitis without worsening fibrosis, fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening steatohepatitis, or both.
insights.validation_note: Verified in handout text lines 1440-1496; page marker shows Page 24.

insights.insight_title: Zepbound OSA coverage excludes diabetes and requires CPAP plus weight-management failure
insights.why_it_matters: Even with an OSA indication, coverage is narrowed to non-diabetic patients after documented specialist involvement, PSG-defined disease, six months of comprehensive weight management, and six months of CPAP failure.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Initial OSA criteria require specialist prescribing/consult, moderate to severe OSA with AHI >15 by attended sleep study or PSG, no type 2 diabetes, BMI at least 30 with a comorbidity, six months of comprehensive weight management including pharmacotherapy, and failed six-month CPAP trial. Renewal requires at least 20% AHI decrease, remission/mild non-symptomatic OSA, or at least 10% weight loss.
insights.validation_note: Verified in handout text lines 1377-1415; page markers show Pages 22-23.

insights.insight_title: Primary biliary cholangitis agents require biopsy, ursodiol failure, alcohol testing, and lab-defined renewal
insights.why_it_matters: Evidence strategy needs to address diagnostic confirmation and objective biochemical response, not only FDA label alignment or symptom burden.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Initial criteria for non-preferred Iqirvo, Livdelzi, and Ocaliva require FDA-label use, hepatologist or gastroenterologist prescribing/consult, liver-biopsy confirmation, no terminal diagnosis, no decompensated cirrhosis, at least six months of ursodiol failure with ALP >1.67x ULN or bilirubin >ULN, and alcohol testing if alcohol use occurred within five years. Renewal requires ALP/bilirubin response or, for Livdelzi, itch benefit after failed cholestyramine, rifampin, and naltrexone.
insights.validation_note: Verified in handout text lines 2695-2735; page markers show Pages 39-40.

insights.insight_title: GLP-1 weight-management coverage was reinstated off-cycle but still split preferred versus non-preferred access
insights.why_it_matters: Coverage shifts can occur outside scheduled reviews, but Zepbound and Saxenda remained non-preferred products requiring trial-and-failure and clinical criteria.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: January 2026 minutes state that, under the Governor's directive, NC Medicaid coverage for GLP-1s for obesity was reinstated effective Dec. 12, 2025, reverting to criteria in place as of Sept. 30, 2025. Wegovy was added back as preferred, while Zepbound and Saxenda were added back as non-preferred and were to be reviewed at the April PDL panel meeting.
insights.validation_note: Verified in minutes text lines 78-89; page marker shows Page 2.

insights.insight_title: Public hearing testimony requires 48-hour notice and written materials are capped at five pages
insights.why_it_matters: New Hampshire's public hearing gives a clear but narrow engagement window before DUR review: speakers must preregister 48 hours ahead, speaking is limited to 3-5 minutes, and written materials must arrive 48 hours ahead and stay under 5 pages.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The September 2025 agenda says the public hearing solicits views on NH Medicaid FFS pharmacy PA criteria; commenters must notify DHHS at least 48 hours in advance, speaking is limited to 3-5 minutes depending on preregistered speakers, and written material must be received at least 48 hours in advance and may not exceed 5 pages.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in New Hampshire September 23, 2025 DUR agenda; similar language appears in the April 2026 agenda.

insights.insight_title: Nebraska's PDL economics are reviewed alongside explicit rebate and savings reports
insights.why_it_matters: Nebraska discloses a structured clinical-then-economic process: rebates matter especially when drugs are therapeutically equivalent, and PBM reporting includes quarterly rebate status, PDL compliance, and savings.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Nebraska guidelines say preferred drugs are based on clinical effectiveness, safety, and outcomes; when drugs are therapeutically equivalent or nearly equivalent, cost including rebates is considered. Economic analysis uses Nebraska utilization, CMS rebates, and supplemental rebates; PBM provides quarterly rebate-agreement status, PDL compliance, and savings reports.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Nebraska PDL Guidelines.

insights.insight_title: Wegovy MASH coverage requires objective fibrosis evidence and long-cycle renewal proof
insights.why_it_matters: Montana's criteria create a high-evidence renewal burden for MASH use: adults need noncirrhotic MASH with F2-F3 fibrosis documented by FibroScan-like ultrasound or biopsy, and renewal requires improvement/no worsening at 12 months and at least every 4 years thereafter.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: For MASH, members must be adults with noncirrhotic MASH and F2-F3 fibrosis diagnosed by specialized ultrasound or liver biopsy, have diet/exercise/lifestyle modification, use a gastroenterology/hepatology specialist or consult, and at renewal provide improvement/no worsening documentation by specialized ultrasound or biopsy.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Montana November 2025 DUR/Formulary meeting material.

insights.insight_title: DPAC public comment is three minutes per medication, with manufacturers capped in aggregate
insights.why_it_matters: Missouri's DPAC page exposes both the timing and tactical limit for manufacturer testimony; the same page publishes quarterly class-edit proposal links that can identify upcoming review categories before decisions are finalized.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The meeting-materials page says any interested party may provide clinically relevant public comment for up to 3 minutes per medication under review, registration must be completed before the meeting, and manufacturers receive 3 minutes in the aggregate per medication.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Missouri DPAC meeting materials page; HTML source has no page number.

insights.insight_title: Anti-obesity GLP-1 criteria embed concurrency blocks and 6-month renewal gates
insights.drug_or_class: Anti-obesity agents, including Wegovy, Saxenda, and Zepbound
insights.why_it_matters: Manufacturers may focus on initial BMI criteria and miss the utilization-management details that can limit persistence: no concurrent weight-loss drug, no concurrent DPP-4 inhibitor with anti-obesity GLP-1s, documented height/weight/BMI, and proof of maintained weight loss for renewal.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Initial criteria require attestation against concurrent weight-loss drugs and against using Wegovy, Saxenda, or Zepbound with a DPP-4 inhibitor. Adult renewal requires documentation of maintained weight loss of at least 5% from baseline; initial and renewal approvals are each 6 months.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in the June 3, 2025 Michigan P&T materials under Anti-Obesity Agents PA criteria revision; renewal language continues on page 10.

insights.insight_title: Michigan will narrow anti-obesity GLP-1 authorization to morbid obesity on January 1, 2026
insights.why_it_matters: This creates a concrete pull-through and reauthorization risk date for existing and prospective Wegovy/Zepbound/Saxenda access, while preserving approved prior authorizations only through the rest of their 6-month term.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: MDHHS reported it would revise coverage policies to limit anti-obesity GLP-1 receptor agonists exclusively to individuals classified as morbidly obese, effective 1/1/2026; existing PAs approved before 1/1/2026 would be honored for the remainder of the 6-month authorization.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in December 2, 2025 draft minutes embedded in the March 3, 2026 Michigan P&T packet.

insights.insight_title: Outcomes-based contracting preferences are explicit and contactable
insights.therapeutic_area: High-cost drugs / gene and specialty therapies
insights.drug_or_class: Zolgensma, Mavyret, Zynteglo, Lyfgenia, Casgevy, Elevidys and other high-cost drugs
insights.why_it_matters: Michigan discloses the kinds of outcomes arrangements it prefers, making this a rare public roadmap for value-based contracting approaches and manufacturer outreach.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: MDHHS says it has CMS approval to pursue outcomes/value-based purchasing for high-cost drugs, lists six active agreements, prefers MDHHS staff tracking outcomes instead of third-party aggregators, and prefers outcomes trackable through claims data, such as small orphan populations or volume/adherence outcomes.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Michigan P&T materials; the later December 2025 minutes repeat the six active agreements and same preferences.

insights.insight_title: Kentucky's Brinsupri access requires CT-confirmed non-CF bronchiectasis plus exacerbation history and smoking attestation
insights.why_it_matters: The final criteria require objective confirmation and specialist involvement, then segment adult and adolescent exacerbation thresholds differently; this is a concrete adoption barrier for a new pulmonary product.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Kentucky's Commissioner decision lists Brinsupri as Non-PDL, with 6-month initial and 12-month renewal duration. Criteria require non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis confirmed by chest CT, specialist prescribing/consultation, at least 2 exacerbations for adults or at least 1 for ages 12-17, antibiotic-treated exacerbations in the past 12 months, and a current-smoker attestation/counseling condition; quantity limit is 1 tablet per day.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 21-66; extracted PDF text has repeated headers but no explicit page marker.

insights.insight_title: Kansas added Journavx to PA after seeing likely off-label chronic-pain use and narrowed the supply limit to each episode
insights.why_it_matters: The Board's rationale shows how early claims surveillance can harden criteria: chronic-pain diagnosis signals triggered concern, and the final amended criteria clarify the 14-day supply limit per acute pain incident or episode.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Kansas minutes say Journavx was added to the list of agents requiring PA; Vertex requested unrestricted access; the state said most requests were potentially off-label because patients had chronic-pain diagnosis codes or other pain-medication claims; the Board recommended specifying that the 14-day supply limit is per incident or episode.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 239-260; page marker is Page3 at line 190.

insights.insight_title: Kansas approved Kebilidi AADC gene therapy PA but scheduled a 2026 revisit after manufacturer objections
insights.why_it_matters: Even for ultra-rare gene therapy, Kansas may approve criteria while leaving a future review window open when manufacturers argue criteria exceed FDA labeling or impose step therapy.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: For AADC Deficiency Gene Therapy Agents, Kansas proposed PA criteria to ensure FDA-label appropriate use; PTC Therapeutics requested criteria without step therapy and additional restrictions beyond FDA labeling; the Board requested review at the October 2026 DUR meeting and approved the criteria unanimously.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 243-271; page marker is Page3 at line 192.

insights.insight_title: Illinois explicitly separates evidence-based D&T recommendations from net economic PDL choices
insights.why_it_matters: A product can survive clinical comparison yet lose on net economics; the public Board process is clinical, while HFS incorporates supplemental rebates and utilization-shift savings.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Illinois states that if safety, effectiveness, and outcomes show no therapeutic advantage, HFS considers net economic impact; the D&T Board bases review and recommendations on evidence-based clinical information, not cost; HFS also cites $82 million in FY2018 supplemental rebates and savings from shifting utilization.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insights.insight_title: Georgia generally waits six months post-market before DURB new-drug review, then allows a narrow manufacturer appeal window after quarterly meetings
insights.drug_or_class: New drugs and supplemental rebate classes
insights.why_it_matters: Launch teams should not only watch meeting dates; Georgia exposes a pre-meeting forum, a roughly 30-day posting window, and a 10-business-day post-meeting appeal channel to GDCH before final decisions settle.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The Georgia handout says new entities are generally not reviewed until on the market at least six months, drugs/classes under review are posted approximately 30 days before the Manufacturers' Forum, DURB recommendations go to GDCH for final decisions, and manufacturers may request an appeal meeting within 10 business days after each quarterly DURB meeting.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 749-802; page marker is Page 11.

insights.insight_title: Connecticut's topical antipsoriatic rules make samples unusable as step-therapy proof and require recent preferred-class trials
insights.drug_or_class: Topical antipsoriatics; Zoryve 0.3% cream; calcipotriene/calcitriol products
insights.why_it_matters: Commercial sampling may not help patients meet Medicaid criteria; documentation must show claims or chart-note evidence of preferred therapy, and formulation-level preferences can override brand/generic assumptions.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The criteria state samples do not meet step therapy or continuation requirements, prior therapies are verified through claims/chart notes, brand-vs-generic exceptions need documented medical reasons, and Zoryve cream requires plaque psoriasis plus trial/failure of one preferred topical vitamin D analog or topical corticosteroid within the previous six months.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 125-153 and 167-172; main criteria begin on Page 2.

insights.insight_title: Connecticut explicitly uses cost-effectiveness to set CAPS PDL status when clinical preference is not generalizable
insights.why_it_matters: For rare-disease classes with limited head-to-head evidence, the state's own rationale says clinical differentiation may not drive preference; cost-effective positioning can become decisive.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The CAPS criteria say AAAAI does not specify one agent over another, choice should be individualized, preference cannot be generalized, and PDL status may remain with the most cost-effective agents.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 42-60 and 131-147; cost-effectiveness rationale is on Page 2.

insights.insight_title: Arkansas splits clinical review from a closed net-cost review committee
insights.why_it_matters: Public clinical rationale is only part of the access decision. Preferred status can depend on a separate closed review of state and federal rebates and final net cost.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The PDL overview describes SSR offers, GNUP terms, a public Drug Review Committee for CER/safety/efficacy, and a closed Drug Cost Committee that reviews proprietary rebate/net-cost data before final preferred-status recommendations.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 7-17, 24-39, and 43-52; page marker changes at line 42.

insights.insight_title: Arizona tells manufacturers exactly which reviewed classes need rebate offers and which do not
insights.therapeutic_area: Cross-therapeutic; HAE, LHRH, new drugs, SGLT2, oncology, PAH, ulcerative colitis
insights.drug_or_class: Hereditary angioedema treatments; new drugs; pituitary suppressive agents/LHRH; multiple no-offer classes
insights.why_it_matters: The manufacturer letter is a forward-looking rebate and class-review map: it distinguishes categories where supplemental rebate economics are active from classes under review without current rebate offers.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The January 2026 letter states supplemental rebate offers were not requested for classes including SGLT2s, oncology oral-hematologic, PAH agents, and ulcerative colitis, while offers were requested for HAE treatments, seven named new drugs, and LHRH agents.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 14-40 and 82-98; page marker changes to Page 2 at line 79.

insights.insight_title: Alaska directs manufacturers away from committee members and into Prime/NHC-style submission channels
insights.why_it_matters: Direct committee-member outreach appears discouraged; useful clinical evidence, including off-label peer-reviewed studies, must be packaged through the formal submission form and contractor/state contacts.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The manufacturer form instructs submissions by email to Prime Therapeutics contacts, requests subject line 'Manufacturer Submission,' says P&T members asked that PDL comments go directly to Prime, and requests no direct member contact. It also frames the form as a request for peer-reviewed literature, including off-label peer-reviewed studies.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 10-21; page marker and embedded form page both indicate Page 1.

insights.insight_title: Wyoming's manufacturer evidence rules exclude package inserts, posters, and late materials
insights.why_it_matters: Wyoming narrows what can influence the committee: unpublished/poster evidence and package-insert restatements are not enough, and written materials need to arrive early enough to be distributed.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The PhRMA guidelines require written materials at least seven days before the meeting, state that late materials may not be submitted to the committee, and say only published studies will be submitted. Poster presentations and package inserts or package-insert summaries are not accepted for review. Representatives are routed through the DUR program rather than individual committee contact.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 16-27 and 105-110; page markers are Pages 1 and 3.

insights.insight_title: Elevidys was limited to ambulatory patients despite safety, logistics, and clinical-benefit concerns
insights.why_it_matters: The committee did not simply deny a controversial gene therapy. It created a narrower pathway, which signals how Wyoming may handle high-cost therapies with limited local administration capacity and uncertain evidence.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The August 2025 minutes described Elevidys as contentiously FDA-approved, not approved on clinical benefit, associated with two deaths, on distribution hold, with no Wyoming facility to administer it, and with high cost, safety concerns, and lack of benefit. Even so, the committee said a pathway was needed and approved limiting criteria to ambulatory patients.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 66-83; page marker is Page 2.

insights.insight_title: Yeztugo PrEP discussion surfaced restart and bridge rules that matter for adherence support
insights.why_it_matters: The committee focused on real-world implementation: HIV screening before each injection, restart after missed six-month dosing, and weekly oral bridging for patients away long-term. These are practical barriers and education points, not just label details.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The February 2026 minutes say individuals should be screened for HIV-1 before each initiation and each subsequent injection. If a patient skips the six-month injection and returns a year later, they must start over; if a patient will be out long-term, they can move to a weekly tablet in the meantime. The committee also discussed lack of evidence for better compliance versus daily or weekly dosing, while noting potential benefit for transient populations.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 139-151; page marker is Page 3.

insights.insight_title: Wisconsin limits manufacturer engagement to formal public channels and favors new head-to-head superiority evidence
insights.drug_or_class: All drug classes reviewed by the Pharmacy PA Committee
insights.why_it_matters: Manufacturers need concise, class-specific, peer-reviewed differentiation. Wisconsin explicitly bars direct outreach on upcoming topics and caps testimony mechanics.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Committee members may not meet privately with manufacturers about upcoming meeting topics. Manufacturer testimony should include new information since the last review and head-to-head peer-reviewed superiority studies. Written testimony is limited to three pages, excludes package inserts/marketing materials/reports, must arrive at DHSWIPDL@Wisconsin.gov at least three business days before the meeting, and speakers get one four-minute slot in up to two individual drug classes.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 373-377 and 555-596; page markers are Pages 7, 10, and 11.

insights.insight_title: TennCare removed disopyramide as a Camzyos prerequisite but left off-label ivabradine for POTS to appeal
insights.why_it_matters: Committee discussion can remove clinically mismatched step edits, but off-label indications may still be excluded from routine criteria and require appeal. That distinction matters for evidence packages and provider support.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The committee approved a modification to Camzyos criteria removing disopyramide as a trial-and-failure option after concern that it was not indicated for the condition. When ivabradine use for POTS was raised, TennCare stated an off-label request would require prescriber appeal and would be taken back for a later meeting.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text around lines 2815-2830; page marker is Page 49.

insights.insight_title: PAC votes are advisory: TennCare rejected prior PAC edits on androgen documentation and GLP-1 program wording
insights.why_it_matters: A favorable committee modification may not survive final agency review. TennCare's rationale also shows when the agency is willing to preserve broader documentation flexibility versus require specific program components.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: In review of prior decisions, TennCare rejected PAC's androgen-class recommendation to replace documentation of low testosterone with attestation, explaining that Optum interprets documentation broadly and applies stricter record requirements mainly when clinically appropriate, such as off-label or rare-disease cases. TennCare also rejected a GLP-1 wording change because guidelines call for behavioral intervention, dietary change, and physical activity.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 10490-10505; page marker is Page 167.

insights.insight_title: South Dakota added a Wegovy-before-Rezdiffra step for MASH patients with BMI 27 or higher
insights.why_it_matters: The committee separated obese/overweight MASH from non-obese MASH access. Rezdiffra may face a GLP-1 step in BMI >=27 patients even though the minutes acknowledge that 20% of MASH patients are non-obese and GLP-1 intolerance is a concern.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: In March 2026 draft minutes, the committee reviewed Wegovy injection for MASH and Rezdiffra, noted that 20% of MASH patients are non-obese and raised concerns about GLP-1 intolerance. After Novo Nordisk public comment, it unanimously approved adding trial and failure of Wegovy before Rezdiffra for patients with BMI 27 and over.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 89-99; page marker is Page 2.

insights.insight_title: Clinical submissions must distinguish products within class and late/off-topic/hard-copy material is ignored
insights.why_it_matters: Rhode Island narrows manufacturer evidence to differentiating clinical information for products under review and enforces a specific pre-meeting deadline.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The P&T page says clinical information relevant to products being reviewed must be submitted to Karen Mariano and should be limited to information that distinguishes the product from others in its therapeutic class. For the June 2, 2026 meeting, the deadline was Tuesday, May 19, 2026; late documents, hard-copy documents, or documents for medications not under review will not be reviewed by the committee.
insights.validation_note: Verified in extracted HTML around 'Submission of Clinical Information'; HTML source has no page numbers.

insights.insight_title: Bylaws bar advance manufacturer clinical packets and cap meeting materials to one-page bullets
insights.why_it_matters: The public meeting is not a broad dossier channel; manufacturers have four minutes total and cannot rely on package inserts or advance clinical packet submissions.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Rhode Island bylaws allow one speaking opportunity per company/manufacturer/group, with four minutes total even with multiple speakers. Materials are restricted to one 8.5 x 11 single-sided page of bulleted information, no audiovisual equipment can be used, and no clinical submissions by manufacturers or organizations, including package inserts, are accepted in advance for committee packets or distributed during the meeting.
insights.validation_note: Verified in bylaws text lines 117-136; page marker shows Page 4.

insights.insight_title: Public testimony requires 14-day registration, one manufacturer per product, two minutes, and no Q&A
insights.why_it_matters: Pennsylvania testimony slots are scarce and procedurally constrained; first registration can determine which manufacturer representative is heard for a product.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: P&T bylaws require testimony registration at least 14 days before the meeting, first-come first-served. Only one manufacturer representative may testify per product; if more than one registers, the first is allowed and others are declined. Spoken testimony is two minutes, written materials are limited to one single-sided page of bullets, and there is no question-and-answer period.
insights.validation_note: Verified in bylaws text lines 138-158; page marker shows Page 4.

insights.insight_title: Journavx acute-pain PA is limited to 14 days and resets only for distinct new pain episodes
insights.why_it_matters: Vertex or competitors should frame access around short-course acute pain episodes, prior acetaminophen/NSAID failure, and documentation of distinct repeat episodes rather than ongoing pain use.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The Jan. 5, 2026 bulletin adds Analgesics, Acute Pain Agents to the Statewide PDL and applies guidelines in FFS and managed care. Criteria require therapeutic failure/contraindication/intolerance to acetaminophen and an NSAID. For Journavx, the beneficiary must not have received a 14-day supply in the past 90 days, or documentation must show a new moderate-to-severe acute pain episode distinct from the prior Journavx-treated episode. Requests are approved for up to 14 days; physician reviewer judgment can override when medically necessary.
insights.validation_note: Verified in bulletin text lines 24-35 and 145-206; page markers show Page 5 for the criteria.

insights.insight_title: Outside parties can request an Oregon ad hoc expert 21 days before review, and that expert can vote on confidential-pricing matters
insights.drug_or_class: P&T Committee ad hoc subject matter experts
insights.why_it_matters: For niche therapies, expert selection is an underused leverage point: a qualified Oregon expert can receive voting rights on utilization controls and confidential pricing for the affected PDL drugs.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Oregon operating procedures allow an interested outside party to request appointment of an ad hoc expert at least 21 calendar days before the P&T meeting if the committee lacks clinical knowledge. Appointed experts must be licensed and actively practicing in Oregon and have full voting rights on the PDL drugs for which they were selected, including utilization controls, PA requirements, review of confidential pricing information, and other PDL conditions.
insights.validation_note: Verified in operating procedures text lines 47-64; page marker context is Page 2.

insights.insight_title: Oregon values comparative new evidence over label recitation, with two-week lead time for clinical written testimony
insights.why_it_matters: Manufacturer testimony that repeats prescribing information is explicitly deprioritized; useful submissions need comparative evidence and enough lead time for staff review.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Oral testimony sign-up and conflict forms are requested no later than 24 hours before the meeting; speakers get three minutes per speaker/institution per agenda item. The most helpful information is evidence-based comparative research limited to new information, while oral presentation of FDA-approved labeling is 'not helpful.' Clinical written testimony should be submitted at least two weeks before the meeting, and written documents during testimony are limited to two pages of new information.
insights.validation_note: Verified in operating procedures text lines 128-166; page marker shows Page 4.

insights.insight_title: New drugs can be held to interim PA for non-funded indications or $5,000 claim/month cost before P&T review
insights.drug_or_class: New drugs, line extensions, combination products, biosimilars
insights.why_it_matters: Oregon has explicit pre-review controls that can affect launch uptake before a formal P&T vote, especially for high-cost products and non-funded conditions.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Until P&T review, new drugs may be reviewed for FDA-approved or compendia-supported indication, FDA-approved dosing, and OHP-funded indication if they are in a class with clinical PA, used for a non-funded HERC condition, or cost more than $5,000 per claim or per month. New significant line extensions are not preferred until reviewed, and combination products and biosimilars are designated non-preferred until reviewed.
insights.validation_note: Verified in operating procedures text lines 188-228; page markers show Pages 5-6.

insights.insight_title: HAE PBPA tiers put new Andembry, Dawnzera, and Ekterly behind lower-tier failures despite first-in-class positioning
insights.drug_or_class: Andembry, Dawnzera, Ekterly, HAE prophylaxis and treatment products
insights.why_it_matters: Launch messaging around oral administration or novel mechanisms may not overcome Oklahoma's proposed PBPA tier structure without patient-specific reasons why lower-tier HAE products cannot be used.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The College recommended Special PA placement for Andembry and Dawnzera in HAE prophylaxis and for Ekterly in HAE treatment, with Special PA criteria requiring a clinically significant reason why the member cannot use all other lower-tiered HAE products. The packet also quantifies a $175,984.39 per member-year spread between highest and lowest prophylaxis options and a $13,632.87 per treatment-dose spread between highest and lowest acute products.
insights.validation_note: Verified in packet text lines 6808-6829 and 6835-6953; page markers show Pages 119-121.

insights.insight_title: Wegovy non-obesity criteria exclude diabetes and require cardiovascular standard-of-care plus 5% renewal weight loss
insights.drug_or_class: Wegovy and GLP-1 receptor agonists for non-obesity indications
insights.why_it_matters: Ohio's non-obesity GLP-1 path turns MACE coverage into a tightly documented cardiovascular-risk pathway and keeps diabetes patients in a different category.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Draft April 2026 minutes list 180-day authorizations for GLP-1 agonists for non-obesity indications. MACE criteria require age 18 or older, BMI at least 27, no combination with another GLP-1/GLP-1-GIP, documentation of prior MI/stroke/symptomatic PAD, standard cardiovascular care, and no type 1 or type 2 diabetes for Wegovy. Subsequent MACE authorization requires efficacy/safety monitoring, chart-noted weight loss of at least 5%, and 80% PDC by claims.
insights.validation_note: Verified in draft minutes text lines 1570-1655; page markers show Pages 21-22.

insights.insight_title: Non-solid dosage forms face point-of-sale age edits even when no clinical PA applies
insights.why_it_matters: Liquid, oral film, sprinkle, or other non-solid formulations may reject for members aged 10 or older even outside class-specific PA, creating a formulation-specific barrier for products positioned around administration convenience.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Non-solid dosage forms that do not require prior authorization for clinical criteria reject at point of sale for members 10 years and older to verify non-solid dosage-form criteria; approval requires a feeding tube need, swallow-study documentation, permanent disability swallowing solids, or a short-term restriction such as mouth surgery.
insights.validation_note: Verified in handout text lines 14109-14135; page marker shows Page 223.

insights.insight_title: Nevada's public-comment route is agenda-bound and best used before the meeting
insights.why_it_matters: Nevada gives manufacturers and advocates a route into meeting materials, but the agenda warns that no action can be taken unless the matter is already listed as an action item.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The October 2025 agenda encourages advance written comments so they can be included in meeting materials, says comments may be submitted to rxinfo@nvha.nv.gov, limits comment to 3 minutes per person, and says no action may be taken on public comment unless the matter is specifically included on the agenda as an action item.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Nevada October 16, 2025 DUR agenda.

insights.insight_title: Zepbound criteria and quantity limits passed without public comment
insights.why_it_matters: Nevada's April 2025 minutes show Zepbound moved through criteria and QL adoption with no public comment and no Board discussion, after all listed MCO representatives approved the proposed criteria.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: For Zepbound, telephonic/web comments were opened but none were provided; Prime reviewed proposed criteria and utilization; Health Plan of Nevada, SilverSummit, Molina, and Anthem approved the criteria as presented; the Board moved to approve the criteria as presented by Prime Therapeutics.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Nevada April 17, 2025 DUR minutes.

insights.insight_title: Wegovy PA was revised for MASH, but dosage-form indication differentiation was required
insights.why_it_matters: The Board did not simply approve a new indication; it required the PA form to distinguish dosage forms by indication, which can affect pharmacy benefit implementation and denial logic.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: January 2026 draft minutes say new indication criteria for MASH were added to the existing Wegovy PA form, and the Board approved the form with revisions to differentiate the correct dosage forms with their indications. Novo Nordisk representatives commented on the Wegovy PA form.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Nebraska January 13, 2026 draft DUR Board minutes.

insights.insight_title: Manufacturer submissions must be short, early, clinical, and non-pricing
insights.why_it_matters: Montana is unusually explicit about what manufacturer evidence the Board wants: new peer-reviewed randomized comparative or controlled trials with true health outcomes, not pricing, submitted at least 7 days before the meeting.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The agenda instructs submitters to email written comments/clinical information to PDL@mt.gov at least 7 days prior, limit clinical information to 2 pages and new information since last review, says randomized comparative or controlled trials with true health outcomes are most helpful, and says not to provide pricing information.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Montana April 2024 DUR meeting agenda; similar language appears in other Montana agendas.

insights.insight_title: Repatha MACE expansion still requires two high-intensity statins plus ezetimibe
insights.why_it_matters: A broadened MACE indication does not remove step therapy. Montana requires prior high-intensity statin and ezetimibe experience and prohibits concomitant PCSK9 use; renewal requires positive LDL-C response documentation.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The Repatha update adds reduced MACE risk for adults at increased risk, including diabetes mellitus as an evidentiary pathway, but requires trial and inadequate response or contraindication to at least two high-intensity statins at maximum tolerated dose in combination with ezetimibe. Renewal requires documentation of positive clinical response such as LDL-C reduction.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Montana November 2025 Repatha criteria update.

insights.insight_title: Montana PDL blocks bypassing criteria with samples, patient assistance, or cash pay
insights.why_it_matters: This limits common bridge and hub tactics: Montana says those histories do not support grandfathering if they were used to bypass criteria or PDL placement.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The May 2026 PDL states that grandfathering of medications does not apply if samples, patient assistance, or cash pay have been used to bypass criteria or PDL placement.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed on page 1 of Montana Healthcare Programs PDL revised May 1, 2026.

insights.insight_title: Industry gets a predictable but tightly rationed comment window
insights.why_it_matters: Mississippi gives pharma a reliable engagement mechanism but limits execution: online registration opens 30 days before each meeting, committee members receive reviews 2-3 weeks prior, and industry designees get 3 minutes per drug.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The minutes say online registration opens 30 days before each meeting; committee members receive Therapeutic Class Reviews electronically about 2-3 weeks before the meeting; advocacy groups and pharmaceutical industry designees have 3 minutes per group or per drug, with MedImpact calling registered speakers and enforcing the time limit.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in the May 2025 minutes and repeated in February 2026 draft minutes with the same 3-minute rule.

insights.insight_title: July 2026 provider notice would prefer both oral and injectable antiobesity entrants
insights.why_it_matters: The May 2026 notice shows a future antiobesity access change before the effective date, including an oral GLP-1 pathway signal and a preferred status move for Zepbound, pending committee and DOM approvals.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The Provider Notice says PDL changes are effective July 1, 2026, pending approval by the P&T Committee, DOM, and DOM's Executive Director. Under new preferred drugs, Antiobesity Select Agents include Foundayo and Zepbound.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Mississippi July 1, 2026 Provider Notice; status is pending final approvals per the notice.

insights.insight_title: Alyftrek access is routed through MPPL PA and an MHP pharmacy carveout
insights.why_it_matters: The criteria require operational documentation beyond diagnosis: genetic testing results must be faxed, baseline FEV1 and BMI must be documented, liver tests must be assessed and monitored, and prescribing must involve an experienced pulmonologist.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Alyftrek is marked 'Not a PDL class - Add to MPPL with PA' and noted as falling in an existing MHP pharmacy carveout class. Criteria include age at least 6, CF diagnosis, responsive CFTR mutation confirmed by genetic testing with test results faxed, baseline FEV1/BMI documentation, LFT monitoring, pulmonologist involvement, and 1-year approval.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in the June 3, 2025 agenda new-drug review and public-comment list.

insights.insight_title: Maryland flags new-to-market PDL drugs for PA until review and stacks migraine CGRP step therapy with clinical criteria and quantity limits
insights.drug_or_class: Aimovig, Ajovy, Emgality, Nurtec ODT, Qulipta, Ubrelvy, Vyepti, Zavzpret and triptans
insights.why_it_matters: Maryland's PDL embeds multiple access edits in abbreviated notation; in migraine, CGRP agents can carry step therapy, clinical criteria, and QLs at the same time, while new-to-market PDL products require PA until reviewed.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The PDL states that new-to-market PDL products require PA until reviewed. In the anti-migraine category, Ajovy, Emgality, and Aimovig are marked Step Therapy plus clinical criteria and quantity limits; Nurtec ODT, Qulipta, Reyvow, Ubrelvy, Vyepti, and Zavzpret are marked with clinical criteria and quantity limits; triptans are also quantity-limited.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 16-25 and 141-170; page marker for the migraine table is Page 4 of 36 at line 126.

insights.insight_title: Maine's PDL trial rules can invalidate samples and may require pill counts or urine drug tests for controlled-substance failures
insights.drug_or_class: Non-preferred drugs; controlled substances; brand/generic step care
insights.why_it_matters: Maine turns trial/failure into a documentation standard: samples, overrides, and individual purchases may not count, and controlled-substance trials can require unusually concrete proof.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Maine's PDL says adequate trials generally require at least two weeks; a trial is not valid if preferred or non-preferred products were readily available by override, individual purchase, samples, etc.; certain controlled-substance trials may require evidence such as random pill counts and random urine drug tests; preferred brands can lose preference when cost-effective generics are available; and non-FDA-approved indications require at least two published, peer-reviewed, non-contradicted, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized studies.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 7-33; page marker is Page 1 of 62 at line 33.

insights.insight_title: Louisiana's managed-care pharmacy public-comment queue exposes imminent medical-drug policy moves across CAR-T, oncology, ophthalmology, HAE, and Zepbound
insights.therapeutic_area: Managed care pharmacy and medical drug policy
insights.drug_or_class: Anti-CD19 CAR-T immunotherapies, Loargys, Rybrevant, Cyramza, Imjudo, Enhertu, ranibizumab products, Soliris, hereditary angioedema, Zepbound
insights.why_it_matters: The public-comment page is a forward-looking access signal for MCO policy adoption before final implementation; the dates identify active intervention windows.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Louisiana states it posts proposed managed care pharmacy and medical drug policies for public comment before adopting, approving, amending, or implementing them. As of the captured page, policies posted May 27, 2026 closed July 11, 2026 for somatostatin analogs/GH receptor antagonists, anti-CD19 CAR-T, and Loargys; policies posted May 7, 2026 closed June 21, 2026 for Rybrevant, Cyramza, Imjudo, Enhertu, Furoscix, Prevymis, rituximab products, ranibizumab products, and Soliris; multiple April 30, 2026 pharmacy policies, including HAE and POS Zepbound, closed June 14, 2026.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insights.insight_title: Kentucky's Leqembi IQLIK criteria require prior completion of 18 months of IV Leqembi and biomarker/MRI/ApoE documentation
insights.why_it_matters: Subcutaneous follow-on access depends on a documented IV-treatment history and baseline risk workup; the criteria also block combination use with other amyloid beta-directed antibodies.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The P&T recommendations require MCI due to Alzheimer's disease or mild AD dementia, specialist involvement, completion of 18 months of IV Leqembi, prior confirmation of beta-amyloid plaques, baseline MMSE/MoCA/CDR, brain MRI, ApoE e4 genotype testing, no combination with other amyloid beta-directed antibodies, and renewal based on stabilization or slowing of decline; age limit is 50-90 and QL is one syringe per week.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 216-286; extracted PDF text has page footer numbers but no explicit page marker near the full passage.

insights.insight_title: Iowa gives manufacturers five minutes and rejects data-on-file in P&T public comment
insights.why_it_matters: Iowa's rules reward concise, peer-reviewed clinical and health-economics evidence submitted in advance; marketing material, late evidence, and data-on-file cannot carry the argument.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Iowa requires sign-up in advance for in-person public comment, limits manufacturer speakers and product lines to 5 minutes, requests clinical and health economics data rather than marketing, asks for a one-page product synopsis and referenced data at least one week before the meeting, and says data-on-file or submitted-for-review articles should not be referenced.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insights.insight_title: Indiana bars MCOs from using more restrictive pharmacy criteria than the statewide Medicaid standard
insights.drug_or_class: SUPDL, non-SUPDL, OTC and carved-out drugs
insights.why_it_matters: Indiana's managed care rule is both an access guardrail and a carve-out playbook: it limits MCO restrictiveness while allowing the state to pull drugs from capitation for rebate, PA-alignment, orphan-drug, and solvency reasons.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The rule says MCOs must follow the SUPDL, allow at least a 72-hour emergency supply without PA, may not use more restrictive criteria including quantitative and nonquantitative limits, and that drugs may be delivered outside capitation for clinical or financial reasons including substantial supplemental rebates, PA alignment issues, orphan/orphan-like drugs, capitation waste, reinsurance, disproportionate use, and MCO requests.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insights.insight_title: Illinois' January 2026 CGRP review split clinical evidence and rebate submissions into separate channels
insights.why_it_matters: The class-review page is a live signal that migraine economics and clinical evidence are being handled in parallel but distinct pathways.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The class review schedule lists CGRP for the January 8, 2026 D&T Advisory Board meeting and directs financial submissions to the supplemental rebate program email while clinical submissions go to the D&T Advisory Board email.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insights.insight_title: Hawaii is moving Zolgensma back into MCO capitation on January 1, 2026
insights.why_it_matters: A gene therapy that was treated as exceptional is being normalized into MCO financial responsibility, so access strategy may need to shift from state carve-out monitoring to plan-level capitation and utilization-management engagement.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The DUR minutes state that the ultra high-cost drug Zolgensma for SMA will be carved back to the MCOs effective January 1, 2026 because other high-cost drugs are now marketed and Zolgensma is no longer unique; the actuary factored it into each of the five MCO capitation rates.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 134-148; extracted PDF text did not expose a page marker near this passage.

insights.insight_title: Hawaii finalized a dental controlled-drug edit limiting key opioids to a 3-day supply
insights.drug_or_class: Oxycodone, hydrocodone, codeine and other dental controlled drugs
insights.why_it_matters: The edit is a narrow access barrier in dental claims, not just a broad opioid policy; manufacturers and access teams may miss it if they only monitor pharmacy PDL tables.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The August 2023 DUR minutes say no outliers were found for oxycodone, hydrocodone, or codeine, all limited to a 3-day supply, and that prospective quantity-limit edits for controlled drugs were finalized beginning June 2023.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 122-135; page marker is Page 3 at line 128.

insights.insight_title: Hawaii's Amitiza criteria require five laxative failures and only short renewal blocks
insights.why_it_matters: The access hurdle is not simply diagnosis-based PA; approval depends on documenting multiple conventional therapy trials, a 60-tablet monthly cap, response documentation, and repeated 3-month renewals.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The PA criteria require chronic idiopathic constipation, failure of conventional therapy, age at least 18, no mechanical GI obstruction, documentation of at least five listed therapies, a maximum quantity of 60 tablets per month, initial approval up to 3 months, and up to three additional 3-month authorizations if responding.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insights.insight_title: Florida's December 2025 P&T changes show new products defaulting to Non-PDL, with one Non-CF bronchiectasis exception carrying clinical PA
insights.therapeutic_area: Cross-therapeutic; immunology, endocrinology, rare disease, pulmonary
insights.drug_or_class: Imuldosa, Leqselvi, Brynovin, Kirsty, Anzupgo, Brinsupri and other new products
insights.why_it_matters: The access impact appears in the post-meeting change summary, not just the agenda: several newly reviewed products were assigned Non-PDL status, while Brinsupri was assigned PDL with clinical PA effective April 1, 2026.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The Florida summary is from the December 12, 2025 P&T meeting and says changes are effective April 1, 2026. It lists multiple new drugs as Non-PDL and lists Brinsupri for non-CF bronchiectasis as PDL with a clinical PA comment.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 2-4, 64-78, 108-142, and 184-191; page marker embedded in header indicates Page 1.

insights.insight_title: Connecticut has statutory PA safety valves: 14-day emergency supply, 24-hour deemed approval, mental-health continuity, and antiretroviral PDL exclusion
insights.why_it_matters: State law can blunt access restrictions even where a drug is non-preferred; mental-health and antiretroviral products have special protections that should be separated from ordinary PDL logic.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The State Law Requirements document says pharmacists dispense a one-time 14-day supply when prescriber authorization cannot be obtained, PA requests not granted or denied within 24 hours are deemed granted, prior authorization is not required for mental-health-related drugs filled/refilled at least once in the prior year, and antiretroviral classes are not included on PDLs.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 17-34; PDF extraction lacks explicit page marker, but all cited text is on the first extracted page.

insights.insight_title: Connecticut's 2026 TNF criteria prefer selected adalimumab and infliximab products but preserve medical exceptions for destabilization and indication mismatch
insights.drug_or_class: TNF inhibitors; adalimumab, infliximab, etanercept, certolizumab, golimumab
insights.why_it_matters: Biosimilar and originator positioning is product-specific. Non-preferred adalimumab/infliximab can still clear PA with failure/ADE to preferred formulations or medical reasons such as age, weight, indication, or destabilization risk.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The TNF criteria list preferred adalimumab-adaz, Hadlima, Humira, Enbrel, and infliximab with implementation date 1/1/2026. Non-preferred adalimumab and infliximab requests require trial/failure or ADE/ADR to preferred formulations, and other non-preferred TNF requests require a medical reason the preferred TNF cannot be used.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 14-44 and 404-485; detailed criteria are on Page 3.

insights.insight_title: Arkansas gives a 30-day implementation runway for moves to non-preferred status, but preferred moves may occur faster
insights.why_it_matters: A brand moving to non-preferred status has a defined monitoring window for provider notices, claim messages, patient-specific prescriber outreach where feasible, and emergency-supply planning.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The PDL overview says changes moving a drug to non-preferred status are communicated at least 30 days before implementation, claims can generate future-change messages, and emergency dispensing may cover up to a five-day supply; drugs moving to preferred status without specific PA criteria may change sooner.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 53-69 and 76-86; page marker is Page 2.

insights.insight_title: Adult stimulant access is tied to functional impairment in school, work, or job-seeking, not just diagnosis
insights.drug_or_class: C-II stimulants; Qelbree; atomoxetine; clonidine IR; guanfacine IR
insights.why_it_matters: Adult ADHD access barriers include documentation of DSM-V symptoms, employment/school impairment, and medical necessity if neither employed nor enrolled; Qelbree is further disadvantaged against atomoxetine and preferred C-II stimulants.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The form says atomoxetine, clonidine IR, and guanfacine IR do not require PA for adult ADHD; Qelbree is non-preferred and requires medical necessity over atomoxetine and preferred C-II stimulants. The form asks about school, employment, job-seeking, and limits some job-seeking treatment support to three months.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 15-17 and 76-119; relevant functional questions are on Page 2.

insights.insight_title: Spravato was recommended preferred in Arizona's January 2026 antidepressant review with no grandfathering
insights.why_it_matters: For treatment-resistant depression strategy, Spravato appears on the recommended preferred list, but the slide flags no grandfathering, so implementation details and PA criteria still matter.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The recommendation slides list Spravato nasal under preferred products for Antidepressants, Other and mark Grandfathering as No.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 34-58; page marker is Page 4.

insights.insight_title: Vanrafia was tied to background supportive care and cost analysis because outcomes data were lacking
insights.why_it_matters: Accelerated approval based on a surrogate endpoint did not block access, but it shaped the committee's motion: indication-limited coverage, background supportive care, and referral for cost analysis.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The minutes state Vanrafia received accelerated approval, should be added to supportive care with RAS inhibitor plus or minus SGLT2, and had data based on decreased proteinuria but no clinical outcomes data. The committee moved to limit to indication with background supportive care and refer for cost analysis.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 100-112; page marker is Page 3.

insights.insight_title: Botox migraine use is now sequenced after CGRP/gepant therapy, with combination allowed only above a headache threshold
insights.drug_or_class: Botox; CGRP antagonists; gepants including Qulipta
insights.why_it_matters: The state moved away from Botox-first combination logic and defined when combination therapy is appropriate, which can affect sequencing strategy for migraine preventives.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The November 2025 minutes say the committee required a 12-week trial of a CGRP or gepant before Botox. If a patient still has more than four headaches per month on the CGRP or gepant, combination therapy with Botox would be appropriate.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 107-117; page marker is Page 3.

insights.insight_title: Narcolepsy agents Sunosi and Wakix have a cumulative 30-day failure ladder
insights.why_it_matters: For wake-promoting brands, access is not a simple preferred/nonpreferred split. Wakix sits behind armodafinil, modafinil, and Sunosi failures, which can extend time to therapy.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The PDL notes Sunosi is approvable only with documentation of treatment failure after 30-day trials of both armodafinil and modafinil. Wakix is approvable only with documentation of treatment failure after 30-day trials of armodafinil, modafinil, and Sunosi.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 5477-5491; page marker is Page 61.

insights.insight_title: Vermont flags GLP-1 spend growth but maintains no weight-loss drug coverage under its State Plan
insights.drug_or_class: GLP-1 receptor agonists including Ozempic, Trulicity, and Mounjaro
insights.why_it_matters: The state is absorbing GLP-1 spend for covered indications while explicitly excluding weight-loss use. New indications such as OSA and metabolic dysfunction may be assessed against this cost-control backdrop.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Vermont reported GLP-1s as the fourth-ranked therapeutic class by gross spend, with $16.9 million gross spend in SFY25 and Ozempic gross costs up 20% over SFY24. The report notes GLP-1s have new indications such as obstructive sleep apnea and noncirrhotic metabolic dysfunction, but Vermont Medicaid does not cover drugs used for weight loss under the Medicaid State Plan.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 125-133 and 191-197; page markers are Pages 3-4.

insights.insight_title: Utah combines strict conflict rules with tightly managed public testimony
insights.why_it_matters: Utah's process is structurally insulated from manufacturer influence: committee members must be independent from pharma manufacturing, and public testimony is compressed unless solicited expert testimony is scheduled in advance.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The bylaws require committee members to have no direct connection to and be independent of the pharmaceutical manufacturing industry for at least five years. Public testimony requires conflict-of-interest disclosure, only one person per organization may testify, unsolicited testimony is generally limited to three minutes, and solicited expert testimony must be scheduled at least seven days before the meeting.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 113-160; page markers are Pages 3-4.

insights.insight_title: TennCare distinguishes 'documentation' from provider attestation in PA criteria
insights.drug_or_class: All TennCare PA criteria using documentation or attestation terms
insights.why_it_matters: A pharma access team should not treat all criteria wording as equal: criteria that say documentation can require chart notes, labs, or other records, while attestation-only criteria can be satisfied by provider confirmation without supporting attachments.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: TennCare clarified that 'Documentation' or 'documented' means written documentation may be required, such as chart notes or lab values, attached to the ePA case or faxed. If the criterion says 'provider's attestation,' only provider confirmation is required without additional supporting documentation.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 53-67; page marker is Page 1.

insights.insight_title: Medical-benefit biosimilars can become no-PA preferred products in South Dakota
insights.drug_or_class: PAD Biosimilar Agents on the medical PDL
insights.why_it_matters: Biosimilar competition may shift on the medical side, not just pharmacy. A preferred biosimilar designation removes PA and will be communicated to providers via listserv.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The March 2026 draft minutes say the medical Preferred Drug List process and initial PDL for PAD Biosimilar Agents were presented. The preferred biosimilar on the PAD Biosimilar PDL would not require PA, and providers would receive notification via listserv.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 70-75; page marker is Page 2.

insights.insight_title: Industry must use the Single PDL mailbox and avoid direct committee contact on PDL status
insights.why_it_matters: The state creates a controlled submission route and bars direct member lobbying, so relationship-driven outreach to committee members can backfire or be disregarded.
