insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The South Carolina P&T page requests pharmaceutical industry members submit information regarding potential PDL drugs to SCSinglePDL@primetherapeutics.com and not directly contact or mail P&T Committee members or staff about PDL status. Committee members must not discuss PDL status issues with industry.
insights.validation_note: Verified in extracted HTML text around the P&T Committee Policies section; HTML source has no page numbers.

insights.insight_title: Medicaid Director must act within 30 days and publicly explain rejected P&T recommendations
insights.why_it_matters: Committee action is advisory, but Ohio has a defined post-recommendation clock and transparency obligation when the Director rejects a recommendation.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Ohio law states that the Director shall act on the committee's recommendations no later than 30 days after the recommendation is posted; if the Director does not accept a recommendation, the Director must present the basis within 14 days after the determination or at the next scheduled meeting, whichever is sooner.
insights.validation_note: Verified in statute PDF text lines 49-56; extracted text around this section is on Page 2.

insights.insight_title: DURB recommendations require commissioner acceptance before claims-system implementation
insights.drug_or_class: Medical Exception Program standards / pharmaceutical services claims processing
insights.why_it_matters: New Jersey's public DURB page makes clear that Board recommendations are not self-executing. The operational access change occurs only once standards are accepted and incorporated into claims processing.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The NJDUR page says the DURB recommends standards for the Commissioners of Human Services and Health and Senior Services to consider for approval; once accepted, those standards are incorporated into the State's claims processing system for pharmaceutical services.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in New Jersey DURB page; HTML source has no page number.

insights.insight_title: Weight-management criteria added Zepbound obstructive sleep apnea and a same-class duplication denial
insights.why_it_matters: This exposes a specific denial lever: using more than one weight-management drug in the class can itself justify denial, even as Zepbound gains an OSA-related indication pathway.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: April 2025 minutes say Weight Management criteria updated Zepbound indications to include moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea and obesity, added criteria for denial for using more than one drug within the class, and the motion to accept with amendments passed.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in New Hampshire April 8, 2025 DUR meeting minutes.

insights.insight_title: Nebraska's opioid controls combine a lower MME ceiling with strict MOUD guardrails
insights.why_it_matters: The barrier is both dose and indication. The PDL lowered the opioid dose ceiling to 120 MME/day, and buprenorphine products for OUD are not approved for pain management and require prescriber and concomitant-opioid checks.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The PDL highlights that maximum opioid dose covered decreased from 150 to 120 MME/day beginning September 1, 2020. For opioid dependence treatments, non-preferred buprenorphine products require OUD diagnosis, are not approved for pain management, require verification of the prescriber's X DEA license number, no concomitant opioids, and preferred-drug failure or patient-specific documentation.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Nebraska PDL September 1, 2020; included because the criteria are explicit and operationally detailed.

insights.insight_title: CGRP migraine prevention requires both migraine burden and two conventional therapy trials
insights.why_it_matters: The CGRP barrier is not just preferred status: Nebraska requires quantified migraine burden and prior treatment history; Aimovig has an additional step through Emgality or Ajovy unless there is patient-specific justification.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Aimovig, Ajovy, and Emgality 120 mg require more than 4 migraines per month for more than 3 months and failure of more than a 1-month trial of two therapies from AAN/AHS guideline categories. Aimovig additionally requires a trial of Emgality 120 mg or Ajovy or a clinical patient-specific reason a preferred agent cannot be used.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Nebraska PDL September 1, 2020 migraine criteria.

insights.insight_title: Maine's opioid policy ties day supply, MME, diagnosis text, palliative PA, and post-surgical duration together
insights.why_it_matters: The opioid barrier is multi-layered: day supply and MME edits interact with diagnosis documentation and exception pathways, so claims support must address more than simple PA status.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Maine's PDL says opioid prescriptions for acute pain are limited to 7-day supplies, chronic pain to 30-day supplies, and more than 7 days or more than 30 MME/day requires PA; cancer, end-of-life/hospice, palliative care, and HIV/AIDS symptoms are general exceptions, but cancer diagnosis must be written on the prescription and palliative-care exceptions require PA with clinical documentation; post-surgical opiate PAs can be up to 60 days with medical necessity from the surgical provider.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 15043-15052; page marker is Page 61 of 62 at line 15034.

insights.insight_title: Kentucky gives industry only three minutes per drug manufacturer and a 7-day exception window after P&T recommendations
insights.why_it_matters: Kentucky's process creates a narrow evidence path: industry presentations are brief, written materials are limited to new label/indication/peer-reviewed information, exceptions must be new information, and the Commissioner makes the final determination.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: 907 KAR 23:010 limits pharmaceutical industry representatives to 3 minutes per drug per manufacturer plus 2 minutes for questions; requires presentation requests 5 business days before the meeting; requires nonverbal materials 7 business days before the meeting; allows adversely affected parties to submit written exceptions within 7 calendar days; and states the Commissioner considers timely exceptions before final determination.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insights.insight_title: Iowa's PDL updates bundle brand-over-generic, 15-day, and mandatory 90-day supply controls
insights.drug_or_class: PDL; brands preferred over generics; 15-day initial supply; mandatory 90-day supply
insights.why_it_matters: Formulary changes are not just preferred/non-preferred decisions; brands-over-generics, starter-fill, and maintenance-supply policies can reshape volume and channel strategy at the same time.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The preferred drug list page shows the current PDL and brands preferred over generics effective June 1, 2026, a 15-day initial prescription supply limit list effective January 1, 2026, and a mandatory 90-day supply prescription list.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insights.insight_title: Illinois keeps all new drugs under prior approval until D&T review, even within an existing PDL class
insights.why_it_matters: Market entry does not create automatic preferred access; manufacturers must plan around a six-month marketplace threshold, a three-week agenda deadline, and a one-appeal-per-year limit.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Illinois says all new drugs require prior approval until the D&T Advisory Board recommends availability without PA; even a new drug in a PDL class needs D&T approval before preferred status; agenda requests are due at least 3 weeks before the meeting; one appeal is allowed per year per product; and a drug must be marketed for 6 months before review.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insights.insight_title: Idaho rations manufacturer access through quarterly Industry Days
insights.why_it_matters: The most direct manufacturer engagement channel is capacity-constrained: one session per company per year, first-come first-served, with agenda materials due two weeks ahead.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Idaho says Industry Days occur the fourth Wednesday of March, June, September, and December; each company may sign up for one Industry Day per calendar year; meetings last up to 25 minutes; sessions are first-come, first-served; and an agenda with topics, objectives, supporting materials, and Medicaid relevance is due at least two weeks prior.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insights.insight_title: Georgia's October 2024 DURB pushed several new drugs to NP/PA after clinical and financial evaluation, including Rezdiffra for MASH
insights.therapeutic_area: MASH/NASH; rare disease; gastroenterology; ophthalmology; nephrology
insights.why_it_matters: Georgia's new-drug pathway can convert high-profile launches into non-preferred/prior-authorized access shortly after review; Rezdiffra's MASH placement is a notable metabolic-liver signal.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The DURB minutes say the Board made recommendations after clinical and financial evaluations. Attachment material shows Agamree, Rezdiffra, Voquezna, Xdemvy, and Xphozah recommended NP/PA, and the listed Georgia FFS Medicaid/PeachCare changes are effective January 1, 2025.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 361-365 and 668-696; implementation list is on Page 10.

insights.insight_title: Xolair asthma approval requires six months of controller-medication compliance, while IgE is not a renewal hurdle
insights.why_it_matters: For biologic asthma access, Arkansas uses claims/chart evidence of standard controller adherence as a gate, but it avoids forcing repeat IgE evidence at renewal.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The Xolair form requires at least six consecutive months of compliance with daily standard controller medications and states the Medicaid drug profile will be reviewed; it also says IgE levels are not applicable for PA renewal requests.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 38-51 and 102-106; controller-compliance requirement begins on Page 1 and IgE note appears on Page 2.

insights.insight_title: West Virginia excludes samples from PA history and sends non-reviewed drugs only to medical-director appeal
insights.drug_or_class: Non-preferred drugs; non-reviewed new drugs; combination products
insights.why_it_matters: Starter programs and samples may not help establish prior therapy, non-reviewed launches lack routine access, and convenience arguments for combination products are disfavored.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The 2026 PDL says pharmaceutical samples will not be considered when evaluating medical condition or prior prescription history for PA drugs. Non-preferred combination products require medical reasoning beyond convenience or enhanced compliance. Non-Reviewed new drugs have not yet been reviewed by P&T and are available only on appeal to the BMS medical director.
insights.validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 72-87; page marker is Page 2.

insights.insight_title: Wegovy was preferred only for MACE risk reduction and still required manual PA
insights.why_it_matters: A preferred PDL position did not equal broad obesity access; coverage was restricted to the cardiovascular risk-reduction indication and explicitly did not auto-approve.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: July 2024 minutes added Wegovy as preferred only for cardiovascular risk reduction. Discussion notes say that even though preferred, PA is required and will not have auto-approved PAs; coverage is only for reducing major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease who are obese or overweight, while full coverage of weight-loss agents was pending.
insights.validation_note: Verified in minutes text lines 578-597; page markers show Pages 8-9.

insights.insight_title: SmartPA can approve non-preferred drugs without a call when claims data show preferred-agent trials
insights.why_it_matters: The access barrier is not just formulary status; it is whether the paid-claims history contains the diagnoses, procedures, or prior preferred-agent trials needed for automated approval.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Missouri says non-preferred agents may be transparently approved through SmartPA after a trial of preferred agents paid for by MO HealthNet. Claims are screened against other drug claims, diagnoses, and procedures; approvals occur without a call over 75% of the time, while non-matches reject and require call-center override.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in Missouri PDL FAQs; HTML source has no page number.

insights.insight_title: Humira loses preferred status while multiple adalimumab and ustekinumab biosimilars gain preferred positioning
insights.drug_or_class: Cytokine and CAM antagonists, Humira, adalimumab biosimilars, ustekinumab biosimilars
insights.why_it_matters: This is a payer-significant biosimilar displacement signal: the recommendation included preferred moves for several biosimilars, non-preferred moves for Humira, and grandfathering language.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: In October 2025 minutes, MedImpact recommended moving Yuflyma, Cyltezo, Hadlima, adalimumab-aaty autoinject, Imuldosa, Selarsdi, and Pyzchiva to preferred, adding Anzupgo to non-preferred, and the committee adopted the recommendation with grandfathering.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in the October 21, 2025 draft P&T minutes; separate Minnesota minutes show a similar Humira-to-nonpreferred pattern.

insights.insight_title: Minnesota recommended moving Humira to nonpreferred while preferring multiple adalimumab and ustekinumab biosimilars
insights.drug_or_class: Cytokine and CAM antagonists, Humira, Pyzchiva, Steqeyma, Cyltezo, Yesintek and related biosimilars
insights.why_it_matters: Minnesota's December 2025 draft minutes show a significant biosimilar-favoring shift, including Humira movement to nonpreferred and preferred status for several biosimilar products.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The committee unanimously recommended adding Pyzchiva and Steqeyma forms as preferred, moving adalimumab-adbm/Cyltezo and Yesintek forms to preferred, adding several ustekinumab products as nonpreferred, and moving Humira kit and Humira pen kit to nonpreferred.
insights.validation_note: Confirmed in December 17, 2025 Minnesota DFC draft minutes.

insights.insight_title: Maryland's mental-health carve-out is drug- and age-specific, not a blanket class carve-out
insights.drug_or_class: Clonidine ER, guanfacine ER, Onyda XR, leuprolide acetate, medroxyprogesterone, Emsam, Ingrezza
insights.why_it_matters: Plan responsibility changes by molecule, age, and indication; a brand may be FFS for one subpopulation and MCO responsibility for another, while still being subject to PDL PA and clinical criteria.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: Maryland says mental-health formulary drugs are carved out of the MCO pharmacy benefit and payable FFS, but some remain subject to PDL and clinical criteria. Generic clonidine and guanfacine remain MCO responsibility, while extended-release guanfacine and clonidine, plus Onyda XR, are FFS only for recipients ages 6-17; leuprolide acetate and medroxyprogesterone are FFS for certain diagnosed behavioral disorders in adult males but require PA through CAMP; Emsam and Ingrezza are the only FFS drugs in their listed AHFS classes.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 7-41 and 264-270; extracted PDF text did not expose page markers.

insights.insight_title: Florida's GLP-1 access barriers are embedded as age, days-supply, volume, and starter-fill edits rather than plain PA status
insights.drug_or_class: Mounjaro, Ozempic, Rybelsus, Trulicity, Victoza, Saxenda
insights.why_it_matters: Even when PA status must be checked separately, utilization edits can constrain titration, starter dosing, and refill cadence for high-budget incretin products.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The limitations file states it may or may not indicate PA status, then lists product-level edits: Mounjaro minimum age 10 and max 2 mL every 30 days; Ozempic minimum age 18 with dose-pen day-supply/volume limits; Rybelsus 3 mg limited to 30 tablets every 365 days; Trulicity and Victoza have age/volume limits.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 7-10, 3722-3724, 4226-4234, 5098-5102, 6065-6067, and 6332-6334; Mounjaro appears on Page 63, with related products on later pages.

insights.insight_title: Arizona's LHRH recommendations preferred Fensolvi while grandfathering selected Lupron Depot pediatric/6-month products
insights.drug_or_class: Pituitary suppressive agents, LHRH; Fensolvi; Lupron Depot
insights.why_it_matters: The state can prefer a new or specific LHRH option while explicitly protecting selected existing patients; market-share impact may depend on new starts versus grandfathered lives.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The January 2026 recommendation slides list Fensolvi 6-month, Lupron Depot 1-month, and Lupron Depot-Ped 1-month as preferred, with grandfathering for Lupron-Depot Ped 3 Months, Lupron-Depot Ped 6 Months, and Lupron-Depot 6 Months.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local text lines 515-526; page marker is Page 36.

insights.insight_title: Some CDRP drugs require prescriber-only PA initiation and clinical-call-center evidence
insights.why_it_matters: Products assigned to CDRP can face workflow barriers beyond standard ePA, including prescriber-only initiation and faxed clinical support.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The CDRP page states certain drugs require PA because of safety issues, public health concerns, fraud/abuse potential, or significant overuse/misuse. For some CDRP drugs, only prescribers, not authorized agents, can initiate PA. Each CDRP drug has specific clinical information that must be provided to the clinical call center, and prescribers may be asked to fax it.
insights.validation_note: Verified in extracted HTML around 'Clinical Drug Review Program (CDRP) About'; HTML source has no page numbers.

insights.insight_title: California's DUR alerts include opioid-specific early-refill sensitivity and a four-prescription additive-toxicity trigger for CNS-depressant classes
insights.drug_or_class: Opioids, benzodiazepines, skeletal muscle relaxants, sleep drugs/tranquilizers, antipsychotics, selected psychotropics
insights.why_it_matters: DUR friction may arise before PA: claims can surface safety alerts based on refill interval, therapeutic duplication, additive toxicity, and alert-priority hierarchy.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The DUR JSON lists active alerts including early refill where refill interval is less than 75% of previous day supply and less than 90% for opioids. It also lists additive toxicity when a target drug exceeds a threshold of four or more active prescriptions across opioid pain/cough, benzodiazepine, muscle relaxant, sleep/tranquilizer, antipsychotic, and selected psychotropic CNS-depressant categories.
insights.validation_note: Verified against local JSON text line 11; source is JSON/HTML-like content, so page number is null.

insights.insight_title: Alabama's prescription-limit policy exempts several sensitive classes but caps many adults at five drugs per month
insights.drug_or_class: Adult outpatient prescriptions; antipsychotics; HIV drugs; seizure drugs
insights.why_it_matters: Access issues may appear as benefit-limit friction rather than PDL status: adult polypharmacy can hit monthly caps, while selected classes have explicit exemptions.
insights.evidence_quote_or_summary: The Alabama prescription-limits page says adults are usually limited to five drugs per month, four of which may be brand drugs; three-month maintenance supply drugs do not count; children and nursing-home patients are exempt; antipsychotic, HIV, and seizure drugs are also exempt.
insights.validation_note: Verified by local text search around the prescription-limits body; source is HTML, so page number is null.
